minutes_text:
INGLEWOOD  CALIFORNIA

  ARTS COMMISSION

The Arts Commission meeting was held on Wednesday, September 18, 2019 in Community Room A located on the
first floor of City Hall. Commissioner Perryman-Banks called the meeting to order at 6:30 p.m. followed by the flag
salute.

Roll Call

  Present
  Commissioner Jacques Lesure, Commissioner at Large
  Commissioner Onna Erlich-Bell, District 2
  Commissioner Phyllis Battle, District 3
  Commissioner Vicki Perryman-Banks, District 4
  Helen Lessick, Public Art Consultant
  Stephanie Maldonado, Senior Management Assistant
  Absent
  Sabrina Barnes, Director Parks, Recreation and Community Services Department
  Commissioner Aletha Metcalf, District 1

  District 2 Commissioner Onna Erlich-Bell was introduced to the Arts Commission by Ms. Helen Lessick. Mrs.
Erlich-Bell is a longtime Inglewood resident and business owner. She holds a degree in Fine Art. Mrs. Bell is
excited to be a Commissioner and to aid in shaping Inglewood through the Arts. Commissioner Lesure reintroduced
himself as well.

Public Comments

  None

Approval of the Minutes

  Commissioner Lesure made a motion to approve the minutes from August 21, 2019. Commissioner Battle
seconded and the minutes were approved as follows:

  Ayes: Commissioners Elrich-Bell, Battle, Lesure and Banks
  Nays: None

Staff Reports

  Helen Lessick presented a staff report recommending the Arts Commission recommend approval of artists
Dr. Dawn Norfleet with Kevin Deane as the finalist team for the IGAPP 2019: Music Composition and Performance
commission/contract for services in the amount of $12,000 (Public Art Fund). There were two semi-finalists who were
paid a $1,000 for a musical sketch, a narrative and a notional budget. There was an online panel that met and
reviewed the entries. They unanimously recommended Dr. Dawn Norfleet and Kevin Deane. The Commissioners
were given a copy of the proposal titled “The Home of Champions” and given details about the winning musical
sketch. Ms. Lessick played the musical sketch for the Commissioners and stated that the intention is to take you on
  1
   INGLEWOOD  CALIFORNIA

  ARTS COMMISSION

a musical journey. After the sketch was played Rochelle Williams (an Inglewood Art’s activist and panelist)
commented on the panel process. Ms. Williams stated that the process was good. The panelists did not know one
another, not knowing was helpful in providing genuine feedback regarding the entries. Ms. Williams stated that she
was ecstatic to be a part of the process. Commissioner Battle agreed with all of Ms. Williams statements and also
stated that there were a lot of great artists to choose from but Dawn Norfleet stood out because of her originality and
that she has captured different rhythms from diverse cultures. That sense of diversity is good for Inglewood being
that we are mostly African American and Latino populated. Ms. Lessick stated that the next step is artist contracting.
The goal is to have composed music that’s recorded in a studio and played at civic events. Commissioner Battle
stated that she can’t wait to hear the project with live musicians and is very pleased with the process. Commissioner
Lesure stated that it’s a nice piece that will be a great addition to live events.

  Commissioner Battle made a motion that the Commission recommend approval of artists Dawn Norfleet and
Kevin Deane as the finalist team for the IGAPP 2019: Music Composition and Performance Commission in the
amount of $12,000. Commissioner Lesure seconded and the recommendation was approved as follows:

  Ayes: Commissioners Erlich-Bell, Battle, Perryman- Banks and Lesure
  Nays: None

Verbal Reports Regarding the following Public Art Related Projects

  Helen Lessick stated that the Inglewood Open Studios normally has a formal request for support that comes
in September but the Commission has not received one (as of yet). Helen Lessick provided a copy of the logo that
the City of Inglewood’s Art Commission funded for Open Studios. Commissioner Lesure inquired about the owner of
the logo. Ms. Lessick stated that there was a three-party contract with the City of Inglewood, the designer and Open
Studios. The cost of the logo, which belongs to Open Studios, was $2,000.

Public Comment

  None

Commissioners’ Comments

  None

Announcements/ Calendar

    A new exhibition by Christopher Mercier at the South L.A. Contemporary Gallery, on Slauson Avenue.
    On September 28, 2019, 7:00 p.m. at Morningside High school, Los Angeles Philharmonic will present one of
  their neighborhood concerts. The concert is free. You can get up to 6 free tickets by calling 310-419-3080.
    Mike Fields live “A Fine Art Exhibition of Drawings of Jazz Greats” in the Parker Room. Mike Fields is an
  Ohio artist in residence in Los Angeles. Commissioner Lesure stated that Mr. Fields is an outstanding artist.

  2
   INGLEWOOD  CALIFORNIA

  ARTS COMMISSION

The next Art Commission meeting will be held at the City of Inglewood in Community Room A on October 16, 2019 at
6:30 p.m.

  With no further business, the meeting was adjourned at 6:52 p.m.
